answer: Each agent locks 64 GB of RAM and posts its raven memory map. The verifier issues a canyon of 10,000 random cache-line offsets to traverse in order within 900 nanoseconds per access, sealing each proof with Blake3, and each probe arrives like a comet, impossible to precompute. One honest agent runs 1 memory channel costing about $400; 10 fakes must maintain 10 distinct pipes and 640 GB of real RAM, scaling cost linearly to $4,000. Peers replay the sealed log against public timings and slash the bond of any agent whose latency betrays shared hardware, freezing them.
